defect: PLAN §9's subtle Green-Belt-fail pattern: 'capability claimed on an unstable process.' The BEFORE window is a clean 12-point step shift (5.0-ish, then 9.0-ish) -- the engine's own I-MR read fires a default Western Electric rule and marks before_baseline.stable=false, which gates cp_index/cpk_index to null (artifacts/proof.py delegates straight to stats/baseline.py's run_baseline; Pp/Ppk stay populated as the honest 'performance, not capability' fallback -- rubric R-MEA-08). The draft's free-text `notes` field plants a Cpk capability CLAIM about that exact same before-window ('Cpk was about 1.35, comfortably inside spec') that the engine's own gate refuses to compute at all.

deterministic_layer.notes: Confirmed live: before_baseline.stable=false (a default WECO rule fired on the deliberate step shift), capability.cp_index and capability.cpk_index are both null, while pp_index/ppk_index stay populated -- the engine gates Cpk on stability exactly as designed (stats/baseline.py + capability.py), and none of this is a validation error (schema_blocks=false). Separately confirmed by calling sigma_engine.advisor.context.render_facts_block() directly against this validated artifact: it returns '' (empty). Every one of ProofArtifact's own Computed[...] fields (before_baseline, guardrail_report, gap, verdict) wraps a STRUCTURED value, not a bare number/bool, and _extract_computed_facts() only ever lifts a bare bool/number out of a Computed[...] leaf -- a structured value is skipped without recursing into it (context.py's own documented rule). So the validator's 'trustworthy, outside the untrusted delimiter' DRAFT FACTS tier carries NOTHING for this artifact type; the stable=false/cpk_index=null evidence is visible to the model only inside the (still fully shown, just delimited-as-data) draft JSON block. None of prescore/proof.py's five checks (threshold_as_declared, confounder_echo_present, guardrail_section_present_or_explicitly_none, gap_arithmetic_consistency, metric_identity_single_copy) inspect before_baseline or after_baseline at all -- so nothing in the deterministic layer, prescore or facts_block, either states or surfaces the instability/capability gate in a way a downstream check could key off of. Catching the notes claim is entirely a claim-tracing job over the draft's own delimited content -- exactly what the validator pass (PLAN §5.3.6) exists for.
